cohort: A retrospective study of 229 diabetic pregnancies (mostly GDM), individually matched for gestational age at delivery with 229 non-diabetic pregnancies.
finding: Diabetic pregnancies showed significantly more common gestational hypertension, chronic hypertension, polyhydramnios, umbilical cord compromise, cesarean sections, macerated stillbirths, neonatal deaths, and fetal malformations, and with double immunostaining, fetal vascular malperfusion (FVM) was found to be as common as maternal vascular malperfusion pattern of placental injury.
mod_finding: Cesarean sections were statistically significantly more common in the diabetic pregnancy group.
